notes: **2026-09-05** — (worktree `rf-imp-E`, branch `fix/imp-closeout-review`) — **BACKFILL TOOL LEARNS ONE CASCADE LEVEL (`RouteRun` → `RouteRunStop`)**, on top of the close-out re-check fix round (base `origin/master` `1ebd4f54`, #623). The first read-only PROD report (2026-09-05) refused all seven NULL-`tenantId` rows, and the five `RouteRunStop`s for a single reason: their parent `RouteRun` rows are THEMSELVES NULL-tenant — two runs, one carrying 1 stop and one carrying 4 — even though each stop’s `RouteStop` and the run’s `Route` already name the same tenant, so classifying a stop against its run’s OWN `tenantId` refused every real row. `scripts/lib/legacy-tenant-backfill.mjs` gains **`classifyRouteRun({routeRowId, routeTenantId, stopTenantIds, stopCount})`**: the tenant comes from the `Route` (`refuse: parent missing` when that row is gone or its own `tenantId` is NULL), and the DISTINCT non-NULL `RouteStop.tenantId` values reached through the run’s stops are a CHECK, never a source — any mismatch is `refuse: parents disagree`, an empty set is fine (`array_agg` over zero rows is NULL, normalised). **`classifyRouteRunStop` gains `effectiveRunTenantId`** — the tenant THIS batch will write to a NULL-tenant run, supplied by the CLI only for runs whose own verdict is `ok`; the unchanged three-way rule then applies, so a stop under a REFUSED run stays `refuse: parent missing` and a disagreeing `RouteStop` is still refused (B1e–B1g pin exactly that). **`BACKFILL_TABLES` is now `["RouteRun","RouteRunStop","PaymentCounter","CreditNote"]` and that array IS the write order**: `buildUpdates` validates every `ok` report in one pass, then emits grouped by the whitelist, so no report ordering can make the batch write a child before its parent (B4f); `--live` executes both inside the SAME single transaction, rollback rule untouched. `scripts/backfill-legacy-tenant-ids.mjs` adds the `RouteRun` listing FIRST (it populates `ctx.repairedRunTenants`, which the stop listing reads), prints run rows with `routeId/routeRowId/routeTenantId/stopCount/stopTenantIds`, and tags a derived stop `(via run repaired in this batch)`; header, `--help` and `--json` all carry the fourth table. Coverage: the unit spec goes 28 → **38 tests** (B0a–B0e classifier, B1e–B1g effective tenant, B4f ordering, B5h CLI source pins) and the DB lane gains **D7** — a second NULL-tenant `RouteRun` with two NULL-tenant stops is reported `ok` + `ok (via run)`, `--dry-run` shows `[1]` as the `RouteRun` statement of 3, `--live` repairs all three in one transaction and the re-run is “nothing to do”. `docs/IMPROVEMENTS.md` now records what the prod report actually returned, including the two rows refused BY DESIGN: the literal `singleton` `PaymentCounter` (a pre-multi-tenant global counter) and a duplicate-numbered orphan `CreditNote` whose derived tenant would violate `@@unique([tenantId, creditNoteNumber])` — a human ruling, not a script’s. Gates on a quiet host (`node.exe` 3 on two consecutive 30 s checks), jest cache cleared: unit spec **38/38**, `local:test:db` **6 suites / 33 tests** (backfill D1–D7 green), `npm test -w apps/api --ci` **250 suites / 4043 tests**, `campaign-check` **0 undischarged** (194 rows / 31 shards / 81 claims), `validate-lessons` exit 0 (unchanged: 39/40, nextId 78), `prettier --check` clean, `tsc -p apps/api/tsconfig.build.json` clean.
